original_question: Consider gradient descent on a convex function f: R^d -> R that is L-smooth, meaning that its gradient exists and is L-Lipschitz. Starting from an initial point x0 in R^d, the iterates are defined by x_{t+1} = x_t - eta_t nabla f(x_t), and f* = inf f with x* denoting a minimizer. What is the best anytime convergence rate for the individual-iterate error f(x_T) - f* that can be guaranteed uniformly over all such objectives by choosing a stepsize sequence (eta_t)_{t=0}^infinity? In particular, does there exist a stepsize sequence and an exponent alpha > 1 such that, for every horizon T in N and every L-smooth convex function f, the error f(x_T) - f* is bounded up to a universal constant factor by L ||x0 - x*||^2 / T^alpha, with the guarantee available in an anytime, monotonically decreasing form across all T?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting Section 1, Open Problem 1 (Eq. (3)) of arXiv:2406.13888, together with the immediately following paragraph titled "Equivalent view: Bounds on the iterate vs. best iterate." In the available arXiv/PMLR version, this is the nearest official formulation; the paper does not formulate this point as Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely. It has the correct optimization setting (convex L-smooth f: R^d -> R, gradient descent iterates x_{t+1} = x_t - eta_t nabla f(x_t), f* = inf f, x* a minimizer), the correct object of interest (the individual-iterate error f(x_T) - f*), the correct uniformity requirement (over all L-smooth convex objectives), and the paper's central question: whether there exists a stepsize schedule giving an anytime rate strictly faster than the classical O(1/T), namely a bound of order L ||x0 - x*||^2 / T^alpha for some alpha > 1 and all T.
missing_details: The paper asks for one fixed infinite stepsize sequence (eta_t)_{t>=0} chosen in advance, not a horizon-dependent or function-dependent schedule.
The guarantee is meant to hold simultaneously for every T in N and uniformly over the whole class of L-smooth convex objectives, with the hidden constant in the symbol '≲' universal.
The paper's phrase 'anytime, monotonically decreasing' refers to the upper bound as a function of T; the actual errors f(x_t) - f* themselves may be nonmonotone when long steps are used.
The paper explicitly distinguishes the target from guarantees on the best-so-far iterate min_{t in [T]} f(x_t) - f*; the open problem is specifically about the individual iterate x_T.
The motivating prior result is an accelerated but non-anytime guarantee: the silver stepsize schedule gives a rate about T^-1.2716 only at horizons T = 2^n - 1, not for all T.
The question is dimension-free in spirit: it is posed uniformly over smooth convex functions on Euclidean spaces R^d, rather than for one fixed dimension only.

No extra algebraic conditions such as homogeneity, polynomial degree restrictions, nilpotency, or a non-real base field are part of this problem; the ambient setting is ordinary Euclidean optimization over the reals.
refined_question: Fix a predetermined infinite stepsize sequence (eta_t)_{t=0}^infinity. For every dimension d in N, every L > 0, every convex function f: R^d -> R with L-Lipschitz gradient, every initial point x0 in R^d, and any minimizer x* of f (with f* = inf f), let gradient descent be defined by x_{t+1} = x_t - eta_t nabla f(x_t). What is the best uniform anytime convergence rate that can be guaranteed for the individual-iterate error f(x_T) - f*? In particular, does there exist such a fixed stepsize sequence and some exponent alpha > 1 such that, for all T in N, one has f(x_T) - f* ≲ L ||x0 - x*||^2 / T^alpha for every L-smooth convex f, where the implicit constant is universal and the right-hand side is an anytime, monotonically decreasing upper bound in T?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as stated in the paper, can one choose a stepsize schedule that accelerates gradient descent in terms of the individual iterate f(x_T) - f*, rather than merely obtaining an anytime guarantee for the best-so-far value min_{t in [T]} f(x_t) - f*?
justification: Section 1 first recalls the classical O(1/T) guarantee for constant stepsizes and then contrasts it with the silver-stepsize schedule, which attains an accelerated rate only at sparse horizons T = 2^n - 1. The paper then formulates the exact open question as Open Problem 1: the best anytime convergence rate for GD with some stepsize sequence, uniformly over L-smooth convex functions, and specifically whether one can get a bound of the form L ||x0 - x*||^2 / T^alpha with alpha > 1 for all T. The paragraph immediately below clarifies an important hidden scope condition: the issue is not best-iterate guarantees, since those can already be made anytime from sparse-horizon bounds, but rather guarantees for the individual iterate x_T. Section 2 confirms that this is the right reading of the draft: Theorem 1 shows that any o(1/T) anytime guarantee would require unbounded stepsizes; Theorem 2 and Corollary 3 show that long steps can create large overshoots that obstruct decaying uniform bounds; and Corollary 4 states that the silver stepsize schedule has no anytime bound tending to zero at any rate. So the draft is essentially on target, with only the above clarifications needed to make it fully stand-alone and maximally faithful to the paper.
